note: The gate refuses a checked field inside a staging entry or a deepen patch, so the refuter's verdicts live here, one per term. A deepen patch cannot carry sources, so the sources behind the Wilted background are listed here for the merger to add.

background: dropped 'for a turtle that held no eggs of its own', a reading of the mock eggs recipe's purpose that no source checked shows.
sources: added Public Domain Review and ckbk for Glasse, Wikipedia for the snapping turtle in American turtle soup, ckbk for the Picayune green turtle soup.

sources: added Acadian Memorial, 64 Parishes on the Acadians and on Paul Prudhomme.

background: the Dictionary of Smoky Mountain English entry is 'killed salad, kilt salad', not 'killed lettuce'; the definition now names killed salad, and 'the same as wilted salad' comes from that entry. 'Hot bacon grease' now 'hot grease' and 'often with a splash of vinegar' is out, as the dictionary says only grease.

background and metAt: no Thanksgiving dish printed 'wilted'; the turtle soup's 'brown butter spinach' is not shown to be wilted. The background now ends on the wilted collard greens the everyday menu of November 2026 set under the Pecan Gulf Fish, and metAt names both.
guest: 'here in brown butter' told the guest what no source shows; now a general line on wilted greens.
open: A deepen patch cannot carry sources, and the entry's one source is the University of Wyoming Extension. The merger should add: Blind Pig and the Acorn, Killed Lettuce, reproducing the Dictionary of Smoky Mountain English (https://blindpigandtheacorn.com/killed-lettuce/); Blue Ridge Country, Killed Lettuce: The Taste of Spring (https://blueridgecountry.com/flavors/killed-lettuce-the-taste-of-spring/); the Brennan's house pack for the Pecan Gulf Fish's wilted collard greens.
The thanksgiving roster's why ('The spinach in the Turtle Soup is wilted in brown butter') carries the same unsourced claim.
